memory_update.text: Add GNRC as an underfollowed data-center backup-power candidate: large-cap but unusually pure recent exposure via hyperscale generator supply agreement and Enercon switchgear/enclosure acquisition.

Add KGS as an underfollowed behind-the-meter power and gas-compression candidate: DPS acquisition gives direct distributed-power exposure to data centers and microgrids, hidden inside a natural-gas compression company.
Add CECO as an underfollowed permitting/emissions gate candidate: gas-power projects for data centers may require emissions, acoustic, and thermal systems before operating permits can be secured.

For behind-the-meter gas power, the investable chokepoint may split into four subnodes: turbine/generator slots, packaged generator/switchgear capacity, distributed-power fleets and gas compression, and emissions/acoustic permitting systems.

Need next-pass verification on private/non-US suppliers such as Rehlko/Kohler, INNIO/Jenbacher, Solar Turbines within Caterpillar, DCL/AERINOX, and EPC subcontractors; many may not be directly investable but can validate bottleneck pressure.

node: Behind-the-meter power generation, gas turbines, generators, and turbine services
summary: Expanded universe for the behind-the-meter gas-power node. The core chokepoint hypothesis remains plausible: AI/data-center load growth is pushing operators toward on-site or near-site gas generation, creating demand for scarce turbine slots, packaged generators, distributed-power fleets, gas-compression services, switchgear/enclosures, and emissions/permitting equipment. Reference lane uses GE Vernova as the obvious gas-turbine slot anchor. Underfollowed lane emphasizes smaller or more niche public companies with direct data-center generator backlog, behind-the-meter distributed-power fleets, or emissions-control exposure. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
